bottleneck: Invasive BCIs require brain surgery with risks of infection, bleeding, and tissue damage — Neuralink's first human implants saw thread retraction — and the decades-long consequences of chronic implants are unknown. Regulators rightly move slowly, but the caution creates a paradox: safety can only be proven through the long-term human use that caution delays. Risk-benefit math is worst for the young patients who would benefit longest, since they face the most years of unknown exposure.
current_state: FDA-approved trials proceed patient by patient with intensive monitoring. Long-term safety data beyond several years does not exist for any high-channel system.

title: Invasive BCI long-term safety unproven
why_it_blocks: Surgery plus unknown decades-long effects confine BCIs to the most desperate cases. Proving lifetime safety is the gate to wider adoption, and it can only be crossed slowly — one patient-year at a time.
